parcels.name: Root title · the whole farm before 1877
parcels.desc: Great House (Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr): the farmhouse with Parcels A and B together, before the 1877 split. NLW Bute D219 lists “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm (107 a.)”, leases 1552–1824.

parcels.name: Lordship of the manor of Llandough
parcels.desc: The manorial lordship (rents, courts, waste), which passed separately from the farm freehold until both reached the Bute Estate.

parcels.name: Parcel A
parcels.desc: The house parcel, whole: farmhouse, yard, woodland and green, about 10 acres (the 1877 split).

parcels.name: Parcel A1 · north wood
parcels.desc: Top third of Parcel A: the woodland (OS 1900 field 45). Later title WA735527.

parcels.name: Parcel A2 · house & yard
parcels.desc: Middle third: farmhouse, yard and buildings (OS 1900 field 70). Title WA240304 (1983), merged into WA231076 (1987).

parcels.name: Parcel A3 · the green
parcels.desc: Lower third: the green by Leckwith Road, village green VG41 (1970).

parcels.name: Parcel B · the fields
parcels.desc: The fields east of the house, about 9 acres (OS 1900 fields 71 and 78; 1939 tenancy plan). Title WA231076.

parcels.name: Woods round the farm
parcels.desc: Woods and land near the farm in the same estates. A link to Parcel A is not established.

transfers.label: 1547 lease
transfers.instrument: A 1,000-year lease of Cydwin (the Great House) from Sir George Herbert to Vaughan. The lease itself is not in hand.
transfers.note: Sir George Herbert held the manor of Llandough by 1545 (rent-roll in Cardiff Records). The Vaughans, a minor gentry family, held the Great House, the chief freehold farm of the parish, from the mid-16th century to the later 18th (Heneb HER). Historical family only. A present-day family of the same name has told us it is not related.

transfers.label: 1767 marriage
transfers.instrument: Inheritance by marriage: William Hurst and Calvert Richard Jones had married two heiresses of this branch of the Herbert family, and by 1767 held the manors of Dinas Powys, Llandough East and Cogan.
transfers.note: Cardiff Records: from 1545 the manor passed from Sir George Herbert to his grandson Sir William Herbert, and stayed with the Herberts of Cogan Pill for several generations.

sources.t: Cardiff Records vol. 2, “The manors of Cardiff district” (Cogan; Llandough)

transfers.label: 1793 purchase
transfers.instrument: Purchase of the lordship by the Earl of Bute (Cardiff Records: Llandough’s later history follows Cogan, bought by the Earl in 1793).
transfers.note: The Bute manor presentments for Llandough begin in 1793 (NLW catalogue, not yet seen). The lordship alone did not carry the Great House freehold.

transfers.label: 1800s acquisition
transfers.instrument: The Bute Estate acquires the freehold of the Great House in the early 19th century; the manorial courts for Llandough and Leckwith are then held in the house. The conveyance, and who sold, are not located.
transfers.note: Heneb HER GGAT02038s. With lordship and freehold together, this is the root title that Bute split in 1877: Parcel A sold, Parcel B kept. Historical family only. A present-day family of the same name has told us it is not related.

transfers.label: 1877 sale
transfers.instrument: Agreement between the Bute Estate and Daniel Thomas & Son: sale, or quarry lease, of the house parcel. The agreement itself is not in hand.
transfers.note: Known from a later family statement (c.1974): Bute sold the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres (Parcel A) and kept about 9 acres (Parcel B). The NLW Bute catalogue has Llandough land “formerly part of Great House Farm” for the lime works, 1876–1912. Before 1877 the farm was one holding; see the root title (R) arcs back through the Vaughans to the Herberts.

transfers.label: 1983 registration
transfers.instrument: First registration of the house, title WA240304, to BP Properties Ltd (Form 1C application, 23 Feb 1983).
transfers.note: Mary was living in the house and died on 26 Mar 1983, while the application was still being examined. Before it: BP’s licence letters of 31 Oct 1974 offered her permission to stay rent-free; she never accepted them, and the Court of Appeal later held that they made her possession permissive. The title was first registered on BP’s paper title (the 1969 WGR conveyance and the unenforced 1962 order). No conveyance from the occupiers is on record.

titles.title: WA240304
titles.why: House and yard (A2). Licence letters offered 31 Oct 1974, never accepted; first registration applied for 23 Feb 1983 to BP Properties Ltd while Mary lived there. No conveyance from the occupiers is on record.

origin.not: Not routed here: WA231076 (the fields, B), first registered in 1982 on the 1938 and 1969 conveyances of land the family rented; WA735527 (the woodland), registered on a 1994 transfer; VG41 (the green), a village-green registration, not a title.
